reason: Adding more cloud material seems a direct way to build the growing central object.
expectation: I expect the core to gather more gas and move toward forming a young Sun, though the exact result is uncertain.

effect: The rotating core and inherited icy dust formed the planet-forming disk, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the earlier rocky and icy material become ingredients for worlds.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the disk brought the inherited dust and the collapsing, rotating cloud together into a clear foundation for planet formation.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making sunlight felt less illuminating as a combination: it completed a goal, but did not advance the fusion question I expected it might.

surprise.text: Planet formation begins before the young Sun reaches sustained hydrogen burning; its earlier light is powered by contraction and accretion.

arbitrary.text: The magnetic-field option's purpose was unclear to me, though I did not choose it, so I cannot judge its result.

continue.text: Yes. I would like to see how the disk's inherited rock and ice become worlds, particularly after the chapter connected them to the growing Sun.
